Your $30,000 H100 sits idle for most of inference.

Not bad code. Physics.

An H100 can do ~989 TFLOPS, but memory moves at only ~3.35 TB/s.

That ~300:1 ratio means the GPU needs massive work per byte read to stay fully utilized.
Otherwise, the cores wait.

During LLM generation, the model weights keep getting reread from memory.
For a 70B model: ~140GB moved per token.

So the bottleneck usually isn’t compute.
It’s memory bandwidth.

Imagine 1,000 chefs in a kitchen:
• Chefs = GPU cores
• Fridge = VRAM
• Hallway = memory bandwidth

If ingredients arrive slowly, most chefs stand idle.

That’s the Memory Wall.

Which is why the real optimizations are:
• Speculative decoding
• Continuous batching
• Quantization

Not more compute.
Less data movement.

LLM inference is a memory logistics problem disguised as a compute problem.
